evidence_scope: regional analogue evidence; surface-soil field transect
primary_source_title: Mars-Like Soils in the Atacama Desert, Chile, and the Dry Limit of Microbial Life
field_locality_and_studied_material: Northern Chile transect centered near 70°W, 24–28°S; Yungay samples included AT01-03, AT02-03A–E and AT03-33–39; surface desert soils were tested for organics, culturable bacteria, DNA and Viking-like reactions.
supported_constraint_or_substrate: Hyperarid, oxidizing, organic-poor mineral soil; Yungay samples had trace organics and very low/undetectable culturable heterotrophs, while chiral-substrate tests separated abiotic reactivity from biological activity.
martian_feature_or_process_dimension: Viking-style life-detection response, organic preservation/destruction, abiotic oxidation and the dry limit of microbial activity in a Mars-like soil.
critical_mismatch_or_limit: Earth surface soil is not Martian regolith; the paper does not match Mars pressure, radiation, gravity or full mineral/oxidant inventory. Its transect and Yungay-area labels are regional; it does not validate every Atacama microhabitat.
host_point_relation: Host Atacama samples are Yungay 24.1047 S, 70.0158 W, 0–3 cm (2018-12). This is a regional Yungay comparison only; no same-point equivalence is established.

evidence_scope: regional analogue evidence; explicit Mars-analogue subsurface field study
primary_source_title: Inhabited subsurface wet smectites in the hyperarid core of the Atacama Desert as an analog for the search for life on Mars
field_locality_and_studied_material: Yungay middle pit at 24°5′5.28″S, 69°54′54.25″W; four additional pits within about 4 km. Surface/shallow soil was halite-, gypsum-, albite- and quartz-rich; wet illite–smectite-rich clay began at ~30 cm and pits reached ~70 cm. Twenty samples were collected in 2017 and repeat/additional samples in 2018.
supported_constraint_or_substrate: A protected subsurface clay/smectite substrate with 78% RH (a_w 0.780), nearly constant ~17 °C at 40 cm, 42.8 wt% clay-size fraction and at least 30 metabolically active halophilic bacterial/archaeal species.
martian_feature_or_process_dimension: Clay-associated water retention, subsurface habitability, biosignature preservation and the possibility of shallow protected niches in ancient Martian phyllosilicate terrains.
critical_mismatch_or_limit: The studied resource is a wet 30–40 cm subsurface layer; it cannot be used to infer the host 0–3 cm surface soil. Earth temperature, pressure, radiation and hydrology differ from Mars, and the paper itself notes patchy habitats; regional occurrence does not certify another Yungay point.
host_point_relation: Host Atacama samples are Yungay 24.1047 S, 70.0158 W, 0–3 cm. The published pits are about 10 km away in longitude and ~30 cm+ deeper; use as regional substrate contrast, not same-point validation.

evidence_scope: regional analogue evidence; field geomorphology/ground-ice comparison
primary_source_title: The high elevation Dry Valleys in Antarctica as analog sites for subsurface ice on Mars
field_locality_and_studied_material: Upper McMurdo Dry Valleys, especially University Valley and nearby Middle Beacon Valley; dry permafrost, ice-cemented/ice-bonded ground and massive ground ice were compared, with ice 10–60 cm below surface, against Phoenix landing-site features.
supported_constraint_or_substrate: Hyperarid polar-desert soils, frozen-water/vapor-dominated hydrology, sublimation and periglacial ground-ice regimes; the two nearby valleys have different cryostratigraphy.
martian_feature_or_process_dimension: Polygonal/thermal-contraction ground, sublimation-related morphology, periglacial processes and surface indicators of subsurface ice at the Phoenix site.
critical_mismatch_or_limit: The authors conclude that surface features may indicate ground ice but cannot diagnose ice type; Phoenix conditions were colder than any MDV site. Host soil is a Taylor/MDV regional point, not the University or Middle Beacon study locality, and no soil microbiome or same-point transfer follows.
host_point_relation: Host McMurdo samples are 77.57 S, 163.52 E, 0–10 cm (2018-01-22). Treat as regional MDV process evidence only; no same-point equivalence to University/Middle Beacon Valley.

evidence_scope: same-region field soil evidence; Mars relevance is process-level and explicitly limited
primary_source_title: Multiple energy sources and metabolic strategies sustain microbial diversity in Antarctic desert soils
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
field_locality_and_studied_material: Sixteen surface soils were collected north of the Mackay Glacier region in South Victoria Land; four named samples are Mount Seuss 4–7. NCBI records for the Mount Seuss soil series report 0–5 cm mineral sandy soil, collection in January 2015, polar-desert context and alkaline pH values; the paper measured texture, pH, salinity, micronutrients, organic C and N.
supported_constraint_or_substrate: Cold hyperarid Antarctic soil with average annual temperature about −20 °C, precipitation <50 mm and very low organic C (~0.02–0.25%); metagenomics/biogeochemistry identified H2/CO/CH4 trace-gas use, metabolic-water potential, and N/S/Fe oxidation pathways.
martian_feature_or_process_dimension: Process-level relevance to water/energy limitation, trace-gas-supported maintenance, redox/chemolithotrophic strategies and oligotrophic soil survival that are useful when discussing possible Martian near-surface constraints.
critical_mismatch_or_limit: This paper is an exact-region soil study, but it does not by itself establish a Mars analogue or reproduce Martian pressure, radiation, gravity, regolith mineralogy or atmospheric chemistry. Metagenomic potential/rates are not evidence that the host soil has the same process; the Mount Seuss coordinates and 0–5 cm records remain metadata-linked, not a blanket regional claim.
host_point_relation: Host Mount Seuss samples are 77.0109–77.0191 S, 161.7417–161.7821 E, 0–5 cm (2015-01-12). The source includes Mount Seuss samples but the paper aggregates 16 Mackay Glacier sites; exact host-sample identity is not claimed without a metadata crosswalk.

primary_source_title: Carbonate rocks in the Mojave Desert as an analogue for Martian carbonates
field_locality_and_studied_material: Little Red Hill, northeastern Mojave near Baker, California (~35°23′N, 116°16′W; ~514 m); carbonate rocks (dominantly dolomite/calcite) carry ~1 mm iron-oxide coatings/rock varnish and were analyzed by XRD, chemistry and VNIR spectroscopy.
supported_constraint_or_substrate: Carbonate-rock substrate with iron-oxide coating that masks carbonate spectral bands and may create a UV-shielded niche beneath/inside rocks.
martian_feature_or_process_dimension: Detection and spectral masking of Martian carbonate outcrops; possible preservation/shielding of biosignatures in coated carbonate rocks.
critical_mismatch_or_limit: Host material is shallow Nevada desert soil, not the studied carbonate bedrock or rock coating; the analogy is mineral/spectral and shielding-specific, not a general soil or climate match. Earth weathering, oxygen/water history and Mars atmospheric/radiation conditions differ.
host_point_relation: Host Mojave samples are Nevada 35.7931–35.7943 N, 114.8618–114.8631 W, 0–10 cm (2019-04-12). Little Red Hill is a separate California locality; regional Mojave label cannot certify carbonate substrate at host point.

evidence_scope: regional analogue evidence; aeolian/interdune field study
primary_source_title: Valley floor aeolianite in an equatorial pit crater on Mars
field_locality_and_studied_material: Pilot analogue field site south of Walvis Bay, Namibia at 23°1′25.19″S, 14°28′5.31″E; mobile barchan dune and interdune pits to 30 cm, representative grabs at ~20 cm, and contrasting albedo layers were analyzed for grain size, moisture, conductivity and soluble salts.
supported_constraint_or_substrate: Aeolian sand/interdune crossbeds with vadose-zone saline cementation; NaCl/CaSO4-rich layers, higher interdune moisture/conductivity and dune migration (~18.25 m yr−1).
martian_feature_or_process_dimension: Dune migration, cross-bed/interdune microtopography, aeolianite formation and transient shallow groundwater/salt cementation used to interpret Lucaya crater “Zebra Dunes” on Mars.
critical_mismatch_or_limit: The Earth site requires fluctuating groundwater and liquid pore water; Mars formation history, moisture duration and the cause of Martian albedo layers remain uncertain. Host material is only 2–5 cm surface soil, whereas the analogue observations were mainly ~20 cm interdune/dune pits. Regional dune evidence does not validate host chemistry.
host_point_relation: Host Namib samples are 23.143 S, 15.207 E, 2–5 cm (2019-05-01), roughly 80 km from the published Walvis Bay site. This is regional process evidence only; no same-point equivalence.

evidence_scope: regional analogue evidence; instrument/field physics at Ashalim
primary_source_title: Microwave remote sensing of physically buried objects in the Negev desert: Implications for subsurface Martian exploration
field_locality_and_studied_material: Ashalim, northern Negev, Israel (UTM 662691 E, 3429579 N); bare fine sand (96±2% 0.125–0.25 mm, 4±2% clay/silt, ~2±1% organic matter) under very dry conditions. A 1 m² aluminum reflector was buried 0–8 cm and detected with a 441 MHz P-band scatterometer.
supported_constraint_or_substrate: Dry eolian sand with measured dielectric/attenuation behavior; field test constrains radar detection of a smooth buried interface beneath a thin dry sand cover.
martian_feature_or_process_dimension: Radar penetration and detection of buried ground ice/liquid-water interfaces, eolian mantles and near-surface subsurface exploration on Mars.
critical_mismatch_or_limit: The buried target was artificial aluminum, not natural ice or water; terrestrial quartz-rich sand differs from basaltic Martian regolith. The proposed multi-meter detection is model extrapolation, and radar signatures alone may not identify Martian ground ice. Host soil substrate and water state are not established by the regional label.
host_point_relation: Host Negev samples are 30.950–30.952 N, 34.691–34.693 E, 2–10 cm (2017-05). The host point may be in the broader Ashalim/Negev area, but no same-point identity or substrate match is asserted.
